solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Senior cleric, shrewd man

parts.note: arch can mean cunning or knowing, as in an arch look
a bishop is one of the men, or pieces, in chess

explanation.surface: A top churchman is described as a canny operator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece here, as in the crossword habit of calling chessmen 'men'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archbishop is the highest-ranking bishop in a province of the church, so a senior cleric.

clue.text: Petty officer material

definitions.meaning: a junior non-commissioned officer, a minor rank
material in the sense of bodily or physical

explanation.surface: Seems to describe the fabric of a junior officer's uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A corporal is a low rank of officer, and corporal as an adjective means of the body, physical.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink in hamper, no doubt

indicators.note: the drink is said to sit in the following words, so its letters lie within them

explanation.surface: A bottle of spirits is surely packed in the picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the letters spanning hamPER NOD oubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernod is a French aniseed-flavoured spirit, a brand of pastis.

clue.text: Get away, pocketing diamonds after a wild adventure

indicators.note: to pocket something is to take it inside, so the getaway word holds the next pieces within it

parts.note: to escape is to get away

indicators.note: diamonds is placed after a, so the letter for a comes first

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: A jewel thief flees with the diamonds after a reckless caper.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or reckless exploit, a wild adventure.

clue.text: Force small lock

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone forces open a little lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' looks like a door lock but is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress in physics and engineering is force applied per unit of area, so it can mean force.

clue.text: Manager sobs, distraught

indicators.note: something distraught is upset and disordered, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A manager weeps, deeply upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is the person in charge at work, a manager or employer.

clue.text: Vigour of Thatcher ultimately shown in life story

indicators.note: the letter is shown inside the life story, so it is placed within that word

parts.note: bio is short for biography, a life story

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of Thatcher is taken

explanation.surface: A biography of Margaret Thatcher displays her energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is liveliness and spirit, a synonym of vigour borrowed from Italian.

clue.text: Trade fair's former location

parts.note: ex is the prefix meaning former, as in ex-wife
a position is a place or location

explanation.surface: Says where a trade show used to be held.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition is a large public exhibition, such as a trade fair or world's fair.

clue.text: Do a mural of erotic nightclub performer? Use this to remove it!

parts.note: to do a mural of someone is to paint them
a stripper takes their clothes off on stage

explanation.surface: If you painted a picture of a striptease artist on the wall, here is how to get it off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'it', the mural, which a solvent product would remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint stripper is a chemical solvent used to remove paint from walls and woodwork.

clue.text: Hack confronting popular composer

parts.note: to hack is to chop roughly
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A poor journalist faces a well-liked composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hack' suggests a journalist; it is the verb to chop.
explanation.definitionFit: Frédéric Chopin was a Polish Romantic composer famous for piano works.

clue.text: Sort of home when seen refurbished

parts.note: in means at home
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: something refurbished is done over and put back differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A kind of house that looks renovated once viewed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' looks like it introduces 'home'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means partly or to some extent, an idiom matching sort of.

clue.text: Greatly reduced exposure of secret agent?

definitions.text: Greatly reduced exposure of secret agent?

parts.words: Greatly reduced exposure of secret agent?
parts.note: exposure in the photographic sense: a tiny photograph of a document, shrunk to dot size, used by spies

explanation.surface: Seems to say a spy's cover was hardly blown at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A microdot is a photograph reduced to the size of a full stop, a classic espionage tool.

clue.text: A sign, primarily, is put in street to help

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of sign is used
is is placed inside the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Instructions for putting up a road sign to guide people.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help or give support to someone.

clue.text: Daughter unfortunately knocked over lotion, dressing

indicators.note: knocked over in a down clue means tipped up, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately
a cream is a lotion for the skin

explanation.surface: A daughter clumsily spills a bottle of skin lotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' reverses D plus ALAS to give SALAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Salad cream is a British bottled condiment, a mayonnaise-like dressing for salads.

clue.text: Cash dispenser in small insignificant place

definitions.meaning: British informal term for a cash machine or ATM set into a bank's outside wall
a poky little room or shop, or an obscure spot

explanation.surface: A cashpoint found in some tiny out-of-the-way spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for an ATM and also means a cramped, unimportant premises.

clue.text: Uninformed, I admit, about reduced number

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the admit word goes around the number

parts.note: to grant a point is to admit it
No. is the shortened form of number

explanation.surface: A confession of not knowing much about a cut in figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorant means lacking knowledge or information, so uninformed is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Nothing left in well?

definitions.meaning: cryptic sense: if all is right, nothing is on the left
well, as in feeling fine or satisfactory

explanation.surface: Seems to ask whether a well has run dry.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means satisfactory or in good health, so well, and read literally says everything is on the right.

clue.text: Most accurate, boy bagging trophy

indicators.note: to bag is to take into a bag, so the boy word holds the trophy inside

parts.note: a son is a boy
a pot is slang for a cup or trophy in sport

explanation.surface: A lad wins a cup with deadly precision.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means exactly right or precise, so as accurate as can be.

clue.text: Point of loud warning?

parts.note: a tip is a pointed end
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

explanation.surface: Asks the purpose of shouting an alert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is not a link word: it gives its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip-off is a private warning or piece of advance information.

clue.text: Mrs T's youth portrayed in satire

indicators.note: the youth is depicted inside the satire, so it sits within that word

parts.note: irony is mocking humour, akin to satire
a lad is a youth

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher's younger days are lampooned.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname was given to Margaret Thatcher, British prime minister, by a Soviet newspaper.

clue.text: Bird, in consequence, turned up over quarry

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so this comes first
turned up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: so means therefore, in consequence
prey is a hunted animal, a quarry

explanation.surface: A bird of prey appears above its target.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey, also called a fish hawk.

clue.text: About to drink gin or cobblers

parts.note: C is circa, about
to lap is to drink as a cat does
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: Someone about to have a gin, or talking rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin is a trap here, not the spirit. 'Cobblers' is British slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is nonsense, the same meaning as the British slang cobblers.

clue.text: Departed behind schedule

explanation.surface: A train left behind its timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means deceased and also overdue or tardy.

clue.text: Religious building in previous year

parts.note: prior means previous

explanation.surface: A church built in the past year.
explanation.definitionFit: A priory is a monastery or nunnery headed by a prior or prioress.

clue.text: Hospital worker, man, unsure heading off for resort

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the heading, or first letter, of unsure is taken off

explanation.surface: A doubtful man sets off on holiday to a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' is read as re-sort; 'heading off' drops the U to leave NSURE before the reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff nurse is a qualified ward nurse in a hospital, ranking below a sister.

clue.text: Pick up that woman carrying article

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the article sits within the pronoun

parts.note: her refers to that woman
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman lifts and carries an item.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a sound or signal is to hear it.
